description: Phosphorus is a chemical element with symbol P and atomic number 15. All elemental forms of phosphorus are highly reactive and never found in nature, with white phosphorus and red phosphorus being the two most common allotropes. It is a member of the pnictogen family that readily forms a wide variety of organic and inorganic compounds.
uses: Phosphorus is essential to all known forms of life through organophosphates including DNA, RNA, ATP, and phospholipids. Industrially, it is primarily used to produce phosphoric acid for phosphate-based fertilizers vital to modern agriculture. Other applications include pesticides, food additives, detergents, and matches, while its flammability can be weaponized in incendiary forms.
characteristics: Phosphorus has an occurrence in Earth's crust of about 0.1% and 31P as its only stable isotope. It has main oxidation states of +5, +3 and −3, with a phosphorus atom containing 15 electrons of which 5 are valence electrons. White phosphorus is highly toxic, flammable and pyrophoric with a faint glow when exposed to oxygen, while red phosphorus is less dangerous.
